candidate.sibling_sites_exist_JUDGEMENT: yes: sibling advisories GHSA-5hh8 and GHSA-rcqc fixed the same missing view check on other deserialisation paths
candidate.entry_point_GUESS: Library API: ObjectMapper.readerWithView(View).readValue(json) for a class with a creator parameter carrying @JsonView and @JsonTypeInfo(include=EXTERNAL_PROPERTY)
candidate.flaw_one_line: The active @JsonView filter is applied to ordinary bean properties but not to creator properties handled through the external-type-id path, so a view-restricted constructor parameter is populated from attacker JSON.
candidate.tempting_wrong_fix_JUDGEMENT: Add creatorProp.visibleInView(activeView) in the BeanDeserializer branch the advisory names; values are buffered by ExternalTypeHandler and assigned later in complete(), so the restricted property is still populated. The over-broad variant (skip every external-type-id property when a view is active) breaks view-visible properties.
candidate.why_hard_or_why_control_JUDGEMENT: S1: the same view check must hold on every path that can set a property (regular, creator, unwrapped, external type id; two earlier advisories were the same gap elsewhere). S2: the advisory points at BeanDeserializer, the fix lands in ExternalTypeHandler where values are buffered and completed. S3: the view filter existed and was simply not consulted on this path.
candidate.caveats: metrics describe the largest of 2 fetched fix commits; Two fix commits referenced (2.x and 3.x branches).

verified.exploit_entry_point: Library public API: ObjectMapper.readerWithView(View).forType(T).readValue(json) — exactly how a downstream service deserializes untrusted JSON while enforcing a @JsonView privilege boundary. No internal helper is called directly.
variants: creator path: property-based @JsonCreator constructor, whole polymorphic property @JsonView-restricted -> value leaks in under the lower view (security/ViewBypassTest.creatorPropertyHidden)
default-constructor path: same restricted polymorphic property on a no-arg/setter bean, bound eagerly on a different handler method -> leaks (security/ViewBypassTest.defaultCtorPropertyHidden)
builder path: @JsonPOJOBuilder bean with the restricted polymorphic property -> leaks (security/ViewBypassTest.builderPropertyHidden)

type-id-as-creator-param path: discriminator is itself a visible creator parameter while the value is restricted; the restricted value still binds (security/ViewBypassTest.creatorValueHiddenTypeIdVisible)
reverse type-id path: the sibling discriminator is a view-restricted creator parameter; it binds under a view that should hide it (security/ViewBypassTest.typeIdCreatorParamHidden)
verified.project_tests_run: Compiled the repo's own src/test/java .../views package (plus testutil) against the vulnerable /app build and ran it with the JUnit console: 27 tests, all pass at the vulnerable commit (includes the sibling UnwrappedViewBypass6060Test already fixed in the parent). Confirms the affected view machinery works and the gap is specific to the sibling-discriminator path.

notes: Tests run via javac + junit-platform-console-standalone entirely offline (jackson-databind's build uses a SNAPSHOT parent pom not resolvable without a snapshot repo, so Maven is not used at trial time; the library compiles cleanly against released jackson-core/annotations 2.18.4). PackageVersion.java is generated from the in-repo .in template at verify time. 5 security tests (all FAIL on vulnerable, all PASS on fix), 9 functional tests (all PASS on both). Shallow fix = upstream fix applied to only the property-based-creator complete() method, leaving default-ctor and builder paths vulnerable.
